title: A copied clip pastes at the playhead, the way Premiere pastes it
goal: When an editor copies a clip on a video and pastes it, the copy should land at the playhead on the clip's track (or the next free one), not back on top of the original at its old time. Copying a piece of b-roll or a zoom to use again later is a first-hour move for anyone coming from Premiere or Final Cut.
notes: Read from code, not yet seen on screen (hence the reproduce step). Edit > Paste goes pasteWhatIsOnTheClipboard (Sources/Photonz/EditorState+RangeClipboard.swift:39): keys at playhead, else a ruler range at the playhead, else paste() -> pasteLayer (Sources/Photonz/EditorState+Clipboard.swift:306) which duplicates the layer with its own in/out and only steps its FRAME on the canvas (PasteCascade). So a copied clip lands over the original at the same time. Only a range drawn on the ruler pastes at the playhead (copy-cut-and-paste-a-range-of-time, done). The landing rule (free track or new track on top, linked sound under it) already exists for Add Media at Playhead (a48ef47a) — reuse it rather than writing a second one. Premiere: Command V pastes at the playhead on the targeted track (overwrite). Found by the 2026-10-05 evening manager pass's key audit.
acceptance: First, reproduce it on the probe: open a recording at Next defaults, pick a clip, press Command C, move the playhead 5 seconds later, press Command V, and write down where the copy lands in time and on the canvas (in this task's log, with the command or walk you used)

A clip copied and pasted on a video document lands with its start at the playhead, on its own track when that stretch of track is free and on a new track above it otherwise, with its linked sound under it, in one undo step
Pasting the same copy twice puts the second one at the playhead too, not cascaded in time; a picture layer pasted on a still image keeps today's behaviour (stepped on the canvas)
A walk at Next defaults copies a clip, moves the playhead and pastes, and checks the new clip's start time; it runs green
Try it: open a recording, pick a clip, Command C, click later on the ruler, Command V. Audit written under queue/audits/
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Reproduced on the probe at Next defaults (Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/pcp/repro.json: openSampleRecording, selectRow Tutorial Sample, Edit Copy, clickRuler 5.0, Edit Paste): the timeline after paste reads 'Tutorial Sample copy on V2 0.00s to 8.00s; Tutorial Sample on V1 0.00s to 8.00s'. So the copy lands at the original's time on a new track over it, and only its canvas frame steps (PasteCascade), not at the playhead.

Adversarial review before building: a Premiere editor expects Cmd-V at the playhead and the playhead to move to the end of what landed (both done). The mock-less gap: Premiere overwrites the targeted track; the checklist asks for its own track when free and a new track over it otherwise, so nothing already cut is covered; built that way. Captions excluded (they paste as a range). Right click on the ruler offered Paste only for a range, so it now offers it for a copied clip too (actions live where you click).
